senses.gloss: m. (כָּתַב) Biblical verse, passage; הַכָּ׳ the Bible text.
units: <cite ref="Chagigah 18a">Ḥag. 18ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>במה הכ׳ מדבר</he> of what does the text speak? <cite ref="Chagigah 18a:9">Ib.</cite> <he>הא לא מסרן הכ׳ אלא וכ׳</he> this proves that the Law intended to leave it to the discretion of the scholars to decide &c.—

<cite ref="Pesachim 3a:10">Pes. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>עקם הכ׳ שמנה וכ׳</he> the text made a circumlocution of eight letters (more than would have been required). Sifra introd., beg. <he>בנין אב מכ׳ אחד</he> a standard rule derived from one verse.
<cite ref="Pesachim 3a:10">Ib.</cite> end <he>כ׳ אחד אומר וכ׳</he> one verse reads …, and another reads &c.; a. fr.—Pl. <he>כְּתוּבִים</he>, <he>כְּתוּבִין</he>. Sifra l. c.
Snh. 45ᵇ; Meïl. 11ᵇ, v. לָמַד; a. fr.—[Ex. R. s. 20, v. כְּתָב.]—Esp. K’thubim, Hagiographa, the third part of the Bible.
<cite ref="Ketubot 50a:13">Keth. 50ᵃ</cite> <he>תורה נביאים וכ׳</he> (abbrev. <he>תנ״ך</he>) Pentateuch, Prophets and Hagiographa.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 14b:11">B. Bath. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>סידרן של כ׳ וכ׳</he> the order of the books of the Hagiographa is: Ruth &c.
<cite ref="Megillah 31a:12">Meg. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>ומשולש בכ׳</he> and for the third time intimated in the Hag.; a. fr.
